area: 2D camera: implementing the measured OG behavior (ledger b-6) in the Phaser 3 / render-only-scene architecture

items.title: Canon camera smoothing (lerp, deadzone, look-ahead) is a fidelity DEFECT here — the OG is a pure position-lock with edge-snap
items.claim: The 2D-camera canon (Keren's 'Scroll Back' GDC 2015 taxonomy) treats lerp-smoothing, camera-window/deadzone, and look-ahead as the quality techniques, with plain position-locking called 'basic'. But ledger b-6 measures the OG as exactly the basic pair: character pins at ~56% of stage width, camera scrolls at EXACTLY the character's world speed (587 px/s @1080 = 313 stage px/s, no lag observed at the 15Hz sampling floor), hard clamp at zone edges. In Keren's own vocabulary the OG is 'position-locking' + 'edge-snapping' with a shifted anchor — so any smoothing, deadzone, or look-ahead added from best practice diverges from the measured original. Note the 15Hz floor means smoothing with settle time under ~67ms would be invisible, so exact lock is both the parsimonious reading and behaviorally indistinguishable at the resolution the ground truth offers.

sources.title: Scroll Back: The Theory and Practice of Cameras in Side-Scrollers (Itay Keren, Game Developer)
GDC Vault — Scroll Back (primary talk record)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger row b-6 (COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md) measures zero smoothing/lag and a hard clamp; per the repo's prime directive, canon smoothing that diverges from the measured OG is a defect. Keren's taxonomy is adopted only as naming, never as parameters.
items.implementation_note: When the camera ships, its spec line should read: position-lock at 56% anchor, zero smoothing, hard clamp — cite b-6. Add a chaos test that plants a lerp<1 and watches the follow lag exceed 0 px/frame (red), then restores exact lock (green).

items.title: Exact Phaser 3 mapping exists — startFollow(player, false, 1, 1) + followOffset.x = +(0.56−0.5)·width + setBounds — but ADAPT to a core-owned scroll formula instead
items.claim: Phaser 3's camera reproduces b-6 natively: startFollow defaults lerpX/lerpY to 1, which the official docs define as 'instantly snap to the target coordinates' (= scrolls at exactly the character's speed); followOffset values are 'subtracted from the Camera target's position', so followOffset.x = +(0.56−0.5)·viewWidth pins the character at 56% (for an 800-wide world view: +48 world px, i.e. scrollX = playerX − 448); setBounds(0,0,zoneWidth,worldHeight) clamps scroll at zone edges, and a forum-confirmed behavior is that the followed target then keeps moving and crosses the screen unaided — precisely b-6's clamped case. HOWEVER, this repo cannot use startFollow as-is: scenes draw at stage pixels via planPose(..., VIEW) (DuelScene.ts, EncounterScene.ts), not at Phaser world coordinates, and camera scroll must feed the screen→world input conversion (stageToWorld), so the scroll is sim state, not render state. The repo-idiomatic implementation is a pure core function: scrollX = clamp(playerX − CAMERA_ANCHOR_X, 0, zoneWidth − WORLD_WIDTH), with CAMERA_ANCHOR_X = 448 world px (CONTRACT, b-6: 1077/1920 ≈ 56.1% of 800 = 448.5) in src/config/, applied in viewport.ts's worldToStage as an extra scroll term.

The Phaser mapping is kept as the cross-check, not the implementation.

Unit-test the three regimes: pinned at 56%, left-edge clamp, right-edge clamp with character crossing screen.

items.title: Duels are fixed-camera and the repo already does exactly that — no camera work belongs in DuelScene
items.claim: b-6's scrolling camera was measured during zone running, not duels. The duel footage is explicitly fixed-camera: src/config/anim.ts cites a 'fixed-camera window t=465.0–466.3', and §S24-C's VS-duel catalogue has the player pixel-static up to 20 ticks between exchanges with all movement measured directly in screen px (no camera-subtraction step needed, unlike the b-6 method warning for zone footage). DuelScene.ts contains zero camera calls and renders through the static VIEW transform — which IS the correct 1:1 behavior for duels. The case split: fixed camera in duels (current, correct); 56%-pin scrolling camera only in zone traversal/exploration scenes (does not exist yet).

items.implementation_note: Nothing to change. Guard against future 'improvement' PRs adding camera follow to DuelScene — the case split above is the rule.

items.title: Never use Phaser setDeadzone — the OG has no camera window
items.claim: Phaser's setDeadzone creates a region where the target moves without scrolling the camera (Keren's 'camera-window' technique, the single most common canon recommendation for side-scrollers). b-6 shows the opposite: the character pins at a fixed 56% anchor while moving — screen x≈1072–1082 @1080, a 10 px band that is measurement noise, not a deadzone (a real window would show the character drifting across a wider band before scroll starts). Any deadzone is a measurable divergence at the anchor pin.

sources.title: Phaser Discourse — working with camera.setDeadzone (practitioner usage)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger row b-6: pin band is 1072–1082 @1080 (≤10 px), i.e. hard position-lock; a deadzone contradicts the measurement. Moot in implementation anyway if item 2's core-owned formula is used, but recorded so the Phaser affordance is never reached for.

items.title: Left-travel camera anchor is UNMEASURED — measure before implementing bidirectional scroll
items.claim: b-6 measured the 56% pin only 'when running right'. Keren's canon documents 'dual-forward focus' (anchor flips to the opposite side when travel direction reverses, giving look-ahead both ways) as a common side-scroller choice distinct from a single fixed anchor — so the OG running LEFT could pin at ~44% (mirrored), stay at 56%, or transition through a snap/window. These produce visibly different behavior and cannot be inferred. The videos contain leftward zone running (§S24-C notes retreat legs, e.g. beach −178/−271 px), so the measurement is available.

sources.title: Scroll Back — dual-forward focus / direction-dependent anchors
GDC Vault — Scroll Back (primary talk record)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger b-6 explicitly scopes its anchor to rightward running; the leftward anchor is absent from every ledger row, and per b-6's own method warning the measurement must track a world-fixed feature (signpost), not frame-differencing.
items.implementation_note: One measurement pass over an extended leftward-travel window in either video: record character screen-x while a signpost-class feature scrolls. Also worth capturing in the same pass: anchor behavior at direction REVERSAL (instant vs transitional).

items.title: Parallax layers ride the camera: boulder layer at 0.73×, plus a fixed screen overlay — implement as per-layer scroll factors in config
items.claim: §S24-G trap 9 is itself a camera measurement: in the A28 forest zone the boulder background layer parallaxes at 0.73× the camera scroll, while the bottom-left mushroom cluster is a screen-fixed overlay (dx=0, corr 1.00). Phaser's native equivalent is per-object scrollFactor (0.73 for the boulder plane, 0 for screen-fixed elements), but since this repo draws in stage px through its own transform (item 2), the idiomatic form is per-layer CONTRACT factors in src/config/ applied as layerScreenX = worldToStage(x) − scrollX·factor·scale at render. Trap 9's warning also carries into any future camera-verification tooling: never anchor camera-motion measurement on a layer whose factor isn't 1.0.

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-G trap 9 provides the measured factors (0.73× boulder plane, 0 for the mushroom overlay); Phaser scrollFactor is the reference semantics but the repo's stage-px render path (src/core/viewport.ts + DuelScene.ts planPose calls) means the factor multiplies the core-owned scrollX at draw time instead.
items.implementation_note: 0.73 enters config as CONTRACT (trap 9); expect more per-zone layer factors to need measuring when zone art is built — one factor per layer, measured the trap-9 way (correlation against camera dx).

dead_ends: The official Phaser Camera docs page does not explicitly state that setBounds clamps scroll during an active follow — that claim had to be grounded via the Phaser Discourse thread (moderator confirmation) instead. Keren's article never discusses a zero-smoothing exact-lock camera beyond naming 'position-locking' as a category, so no canon source endorses the OG's exact behavior — the ledger is the only authority for it. No source of any kind was found describing the original SHS: Duels Flash camera implementation (searching would have been redundant: the repo's P0 experiment already established the payload needs the dead Player.IO backend, so the videos/ledger remain the sole ground truth). Repo grep for existing camera code found only two comment-level mentions (anim.ts 'fixed-camera window', progression.ts 'Rebirth Scroll') — zero executable camera code, confirming the duel-is-fixed-camera case empirically.
